description: Create a local video with sequential v1 clips and nonoverlapping v2 clips above them. Every clip requires track; v2 requires start seconds, v1 forbids start. Crop uses source-edge percentages; place selects full, halves, corner picture-in-picture or a custom normalized box. Omitted crop/place mean zero crop/full. Supports trims (at least 3 frames (0.1 seconds)), fill/fit, pan (0–1), zoom (1–3), photos (0.1–30 seconds), audio and source-second punch-ins. Up to 300 clips, maximum end 180 seconds. after_clip indexes the request array and must target v1; the incoming neighbor is the next v1, skipping v2. Transitions clamp to adjacent clip limits. Captions and pause detection use v1 only, even when muted. Removing pauses ripples both tracks and overlays; conflicting v1 transitions return an explicit error. Align sources manually; no automatic sync or drift correction. Example: put reference.mp4 on top muted, me.mp4 on the bottom, crop 5% off the sides, start together, Clean captions from my voice. Captions are made on your computer in English; optional corrections replace exact words/phrases. Specify caption style clean/boxed/minimal/karaoke/bold-keyword/word-pop/highlight-box/neon/pop-up/typewriter/outline/editorial/gradient/mixed, position upper/center/lower and size s/m/l. Style mixed gives every word its own font, weight, color and spacing; add captions.mix with a preset (creator or editorial), seed and palette, and captions.word_styles to restyle chosen words by source seconds (font, weight, italic, fill, tracking, leading, underline, highlight). Example: mixed-font Creator trio captions with a cream, yellow and pink palette, underline the words spoken from 2.0 to 2.8 seconds in the first clip. Titles: texts adds up to 100 native titles of up to 120 characters, each either bound to a clip (v1 or v2) by clip (shown for that clip's whole span; optional timestamp source = the clip's source in-point as mm:ss, or timeline) or placed with start and duration timeline seconds. Defaults: sans 800, size m, centered, no backing; set font, weight, italic, fill, size, x, y and backing to restyle. Plain titles are free and never leave your computer. A title may take reveal (a rectangular wipe over stationary text) and occlusion (behind the people in one clip); the texts schema gives each field, default and rule, and either needs Pro to export. Examples: “Wipe 'Grand opening' in from the left over half a second” is texts [{text:"Grand opening", clip:0, reveal:{direction:"right", duration:0.5}}]; “Put the title 'Sunday reset' behind me in this clip from 1 to 4 seconds, near the top, with a soft edge” is texts [{text:"Sunday reset", start:1, duration:3, y:0.25, occlusion:{clip:0, feather:2}}]. Rapid intro: rapid_intro takes 5–7 v1 clip indices in teaser order and one label per clip; it prepends a 3–6-frame cut (frames_per_clip, default 5) of each clip's trim, muted by default, then plays the unchanged v1 body with each clip's label and timestamp (source in-point mm:ss by default; timeline or none). Everything with an absolute time (v2 starts, overlay starts, explicit titles) moves later by the intro length, so give those times as for the edit without the intro. Build it in one call. This tool never looks at pictures: use the descriptions the user gives or ask for them, and never invent them from file names. Example: “Make a five-frame rapid intro from grind.mp4, pour.mp4, stir.mp4, steam.mp4 and serve.mp4, then replay them with source timestamps and the labels Grind beans, Pour water, Stir, Steam milk and Serve, in 9:16.” is one call with five v1 clips, rapid_intro {clips:[0,1,2,3,4], frames_per_clip:5, timestamp:"source", labels:[{clip:0,text:"Grind beans"},…]} and aspect 9x16. No overlays or unchanged free overlays with Clean/Boxed/Minimal captions and no word_styles export without login; plain titles and rapid intro are free; titles with a reveal or behind people, mixed captions, word styles and other edits need Pro. 1080p default, 720p also free. Media never uploads; Studio exports never enter account history. Returns job_id; poll job_status. Motion: clips, texts and overlays take an optional motion object of keyframe channels x, y, scale, rotation and opacity, each [{at, value, easing}], that moves, scales, rotates or fades the whole layer over its finished picture. zoom is static inner framing; motion.scale is outer motion. at is source seconds for footage (photos: seconds on the photo's own clock, from its in) and local seconds from its own start for titles and overlays. x and y are fractions of the output width and height (positive right and down), scale is a multiplier, rotation is clockwise degrees, opacity is 0–1. easing is hold, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out or a custom [x1, y1, x2, y2] curve with each number 0–1, and shapes the segment after its key; values hold before the first and after the last key. Example: “On the first clip, smoothly zoom from 100% at source 0s to 120% at 2s, then slide 15% left by 3s; fade 'Watch this' in over its first half-second, in 9:16.” is clips[0].motion {scale:[{at:0,value:1,easing:"ease-in-out"},{at:2,value:1.2,easing:"linear"}], x:[{at:0,value:0,easing:"hold"},{at:2,value:0,easing:"ease-in-out"},{at:3,value:-0.15,easing:"linear"}]}, texts [{text:"Watch this", start:0, duration:4, motion:{opacity:[{at:0,value:0,easing:"ease-out"},{at:0.5,value:1,easing:"linear"}]}}] and aspect 9x16. Footage and title motion are free. Any non-identity motion key on an overlay, even on a free preset, needs Pro; keys that all equal the neutral value (x 0, y 0, scale 1, rotation 0, opacity 1) stay free. Sounds: sfx places up to 100 short effects from the built-in free sound pack, and nothing else (no other audio, music or links). The sounds are click: ugc-click-01 (Interface click), ugc-click-02 (Mouse click); typing: ugc-typing-01 (Keyboard burst), ugc-typing-02 (Single mechanical key); whoosh: ugc-whoosh-01 (Bamboo swish), ugc-whoosh-02 (Air sweep); pop: ugc-pop-01 (Bubble pop), ugc-pop-02 (Mouth pop); sparkle: ugc-sparkle-01 (Cartoon sparkle), ugc-sparkle-02 (Magic chime). Give each exactly one of start (timeline seconds of the edit before pause removal and any rapid intro, which move it with the edit) or anchor: title-enter {text: index in texts}, transition {after_clip: index of a v1 clip listed in transitions}, overlay-cue {overlay: index in overlays, cue: a tap id from that overlay's activeCues}. offset moves an anchored sound up to 2 seconds either way. Optional in/out (seconds inside the sound), gain, mute, fade_in, fade_out. A sound needs its title, transition or tap to exist; a missing one is an error naming the field. auto_sfx adds sounds for you instead: events title, transition and cta-tap, a seed, intensity subtle or normal, and title_sound pop, typing or sparkle; the job warnings list each sound added (variant, owner, time) and each event skipped with its reason. Sounds play alongside the clips, never change their speech volume or the video's length and are cut where the video ends. They are free and never leave your computer. Example: “Add a quiet interface click at 1.2 seconds and a bubble pop when the title 'My three tips' appears” is sfx [{asset:"ugc-click-01", start:1.2, gain:0.25}, {asset:"ugc-pop-01", anchor:{kind:"title-enter", text:0}}] with that title in texts. Caption lines: speech is cut into phrases of a few words; captions.grouping sets how, and captions.lines moves, sizes, rotates or restyles chosen phrases by v1 clip index and source seconds (a range covers whole phrases by their middle). captions.scatter gives every phrase its own position, size, small rotation and style from a styles list for one seed. Moving, sizing and rotating a phrase is free, and so are scatter styles and line styles from clean, boxed, minimal; any other line style (including mixed), a scatter styles list with one, or styled words needs Pro, so tell the user before rendering when a request uses them. clips[].captions_enabled false drops that v1 clip's speech from the captions; rapid_intro teasers show no captions unless captions_on_teasers is true. Build the whole edit in one call. Example: “Use these five clips in order, add a five-frame Rapid intro with these labels, generate captions with a different style and safe position for each short phrase using Scatter seed 58 with free styles, then export a vertical 720p MP4” is captions {style: "clean", position: "lower", size: "m", scatter: {seed: 58, safe_zone: "social", intensity: "normal", styles: ["clean", "boxed", "minimal"]}} with rapid_intro and quality 720p.

auto_sfx.description: Let the tool place sounds for you on the finished edit (after captions, pause removal and any rapid intro), with one sound per event, whooshes only at configured transitions and clicks only at taps the overlay declares. Events too close together keep the most important one. The job result lists what was added and what was skipped by owner, so tell the user which overlays have no tap.

events.description: title (a title appears), transition (a configured crossfade or dip; hard cuts and the rapid-intro teaser cuts get nothing) and cta-tap (a tap an overlay declares). Default all three.

intensity.description: subtle plays the sounds quieter. Default normal.

seed.description: Picks between the two variants of a sound; the same seed gives the same choice. Default 58.

title_sound.description: Kind of sound for titles. Default pop.

grouping.description: How speech is cut into caption phrases (lines): a phrase ends at a pause of at least pause seconds, at max_words words, max_characters characters or max_duration seconds, or after a sentence. All four are required. Omit for the standard grouping (7 words, 32 characters, 30 seconds, 0.6 second pause); with scatter and no grouping it is 4 words, 24 characters, 1.8 seconds, 0.35 second pause.

lines.description: Place or restyle chosen phrases by source seconds. Overlapping rows merge in request order. A row that reaches no spoken phrase, or whose phrases are gone after pause removal or the rapid intro, is an error naming it. At most 100 rows.

items.description: from–to are source seconds of that v1 clip's own trim; the row applies to every whole phrase whose middle, (first word start + last word end) / 2, is in [from, to), so one range can change several phrases. x and y are the phrase block's centre as fractions of the output, size the font height as a fraction of the output's shorter side, rotation clockwise degrees. Needs at least one of x, y, size, rotation or style; mix goes with style mixed.

clip.description: Index of a v1 clip in clips.

mix.description: Only with style mixed. Presets: creator (Creator trio) and editorial (Editorial trio). The same seed and palette give the same look; omit seed for the default look.
Only with style mixed. Presets: creator (Creator trio) and editorial (Editorial trio). The same seed and palette give the same look; omit seed for the default look.

scatter.description: Give every spoken phrase its own position, size, small rotation and style from styles, chosen by the seed (the same seed and speech give the same result) and kept clear of titles and overlays. social keeps text inside a conservative portrait feed area, frame inside the picture margin. subtle varies rotation and size less than normal. All four fields are required. Explicit lines rows win over it. Pro is needed only if styles holds an expressive style other than captions.style.

style.description: mixed gives every word its own font, weight, color and spacing from three families.

word_styles.description: Style spoken words by source seconds: every word whose midpoint falls in from–to of that v1 clip's own trim, after corrections. A range with no spoken words is an error. Needs Pro.

appearance.description: At least one field. sans (Montserrat) weights 500/700/800/900; serif (Lora) 400/600/700 with italic; mono (Roboto Mono) 400/500/700. weight and italic need font. Tracking in em, leading as a line-height multiple, highlight false removes a highlight.

clip.description: Index of a v1 clip in clips.

captions_enabled.description: Only on a v1 clip in a request with captions. false keeps this clip's speech out of the captions (muted clips keep theirs by default); omit or true for captions.

crop.description: Percent removed from each oriented source edge; opposite sides must total at most 95. Omit for zero crop.

motion.description: Outer layer motion over its finished picture: x and y are offsets as fractions of the output width and height (positive right and down), scale a multiplier (1 = unchanged), rotation clockwise degrees, opacity 0–1. Keys are at source seconds of this clip (photos: seconds on the photo's own clock, which starts at its in, default 0). zoom stays static inner framing; motion.scale is outer motion of the whole placed picture. Free. At most 60 keys per channel, 1000 per request.

easing.description: Shapes the segment that starts at this key: a named curve or a custom Bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2], each 0–1.
Shapes the segment that starts at this key: a named curve or a custom Bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2], each 0–1.

place.description: Destination box in the output. Custom coordinates are normalized, contained in the output. Omit for full.

start.description: Required on v2, forbidden on v1. Timeline seconds, independent of source in/out. V2 clips cannot overlap.

track.description: Required. v1 plays in request order and supplies captions/pauses; v2 plays above it at an explicit start.

configuration.description: The relative configuration URL returned by configure_overlay.

Keys are at local seconds from this overlay's own start. Any non-identity key needs Pro. At most 60 keys per channel, 1000 per request.

rapid_intro.description: Rapid intro: 5–7 v1 clips become teasers (the first frames of each clip's trim, no transitions) placed before the unchanged v1 body, whose clips get the labels. V2 starts, overlay starts and explicit titles move later by the teaser total.

captions_on_teasers.description: Only in a request with captions. Default false: the teaser cuts show no captions, the body keeps them.

clips.description: Indices of 5–7 distinct v1 clips in clips, in teaser order.

frames_per_clip.description: Frames in each teaser cut. Default 5.

labels.description: Exactly one label for each chosen clip, supplied by the user or the assistant; the tool does not look at pictures.

timestamp.description: Stamp above each body label: source (the clip's source in-point as mm:ss, default), timeline (its timeline start as mm:ss) or none. Photos cannot use source.

items.description: One sound from the built-in pack.

anchor.description: Follow an event instead of a fixed time. Exactly one of start or anchor.

text.description: Index in texts: the moment that title first appears.

after_clip.description: Request index of a v1 clip listed in transitions: the middle of a crossfade or the dip's black point.

cue.description: A tap id from that overlay's activeCues (configure_overlay).

gain.description: Volume 0–2. Default is the sound's own quiet level.

in.description: Seconds into the sound where playback starts (not video time). Default the beginning.

mute.description: Keep the sound in the edit but silent. Default false.

offset.description: Seconds after (positive) or before the anchored event. Only with anchor; default 0.

out.description: Seconds into the sound where playback ends. Default the whole sound.

start.description: Timeline seconds of the edit as you describe it before pause removal and any rapid intro, which move it with the edit. Give exactly one of start or anchor.

clip.description: Index of a clip in clips (v1 or v2): the title follows that clip's whole span. Do not combine with start/duration.

motion.description: Outer layer motion over its finished picture: x and y are offsets as fractions of the output width and height (positive right and down), scale a multiplier (1 = unchanged), rotation clockwise degrees, opacity 0–1. Keys are at local seconds from this title's own start. Free. At most 60 keys per channel, 1000 per request.

occlusion.description: Put the title behind the people in one clip: it is drawn behind every detected person in that clip's picture, found on your computer with a small people model that ships inside the package. Needs Pro to export (free to omit).

clip.description: Index in clips (v1 or v2, video or photo) whose people stand in front of the title. Required for a title placed with start and duration, which must overlap that clip in time; omit it, or give the title's own clip, for a title bound with clip.

feather.description: Softness of the person's edge in mask pixels. Default 1.

smoothing.description: How much the two previous pictures steady the mask. Default 0.2.

threshold.description: How sure a pixel must be to count as a person. Default 0.5.

reveal.description: A rectangular wipe that reveals the finished title over stationary text; omit the field for a plain title. Needs Pro to export (free to omit).

direction.description: The way the visible window grows: right starts at the left edge, left at the right edge, down at the top, up at the bottom. Default up.

easing.description: Shapes the wipe's progress: a named curve or a custom Bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2], each 0–1. Default ease-out.

rect.description: The part of the title box (its text plus padding) that is revealed, as fractions from its top left; width and height at least 0.01, inside the box. Omitted sides default to the whole box.

start.description: Local seconds from the title's own start when the wipe begins; nothing of the title shows before it. Default 0.
Timeline seconds without clip, before any intro prepend.

text.description: The title. May be empty only with timestamp.

timestamp.description: Needs clip. source is that clip's source in-point as mm:ss (not for photos); timeline is its start in the timeline as mm:ss. Shown above the text.
